exercises.title: No lost update: sell one unit atomically
concepts: UPDATE … SET x = x − 1 WHERE x >= 1
exercises.problemHtml:
Two customers buy the last Moleskine notebooks (CT0906) at the same moment. Reading the stock in the app and writing stock - 1 back loses one sale. Write ONE statement that takes one unit only if one is available and returns sku, stock (no row = sold out).

Sample database: CT Shop mini (the course's lab project, sliced)

customer       (id PK, email UNIQUE lower-case, full_name, phone NULL, city DEFAULT 'Hà Nội', created_at timestamptz)
category       (id PK, name UNIQUE, parent_id → category.id — NULL = root)       12 rows: 1–4 roots, 5–12 children
product        (id PK, sku UNIQUE, name, category_id → category, price numeric(12,2) > 0, stock int ≥ 0 DEFAULT 0,
                attrs jsonb DEFAULT '{}', is_active boolean DEFAULT true, created_at)          16 rows (ids 1…46, gaps)
orders         (id PK, customer_id → customer, status pending|paid|shipped|cancelled, created_at timestamptz, note)   14 rows
order_item     (order_id → orders ON DELETE CASCADE, product_id → product, qty > 0, unit_price) — PK (order_id, product_id)
payment        (id PK, order_id UNIQUE → orders, amount, method cod|card|momo|bank, paid_at)    one per paid/shipped order
stock_movement (id PK, product_id → product, change ≠ 0, reason import|sale|return|adjust, order_id NULL, created_at)
review         (id PK, product_id → product, customer_id → customer, rating 1–5, body, created_at) — UNIQUE (product_id, customer_id)

Same 8 tables as Labs 1–9 (in schema public instead of shop); the rows are a small slice of the lab data — same category tree, same product ids/SKUs/prices. Every id is GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY: leave it out of INSERT. Times are timestamptz shown in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh. Full script: the ctshop.sql tab.

Requirements

  • UPDATE product SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE sku = 'CT0906' AND stock >= 1 RETURNING sku, stock.
  • No SELECT before the UPDATE.

stock_movement (id PK, product_id → product, change ≠ 0, reason import|sale|return|adjust, order_id NULL, created_at)

Đúng 8 bảng của Lab 1–9 (ở schema public thay vì shop); dữ liệu là một lát nhỏ của dữ liệu lab — cùng cây danh mục, cùng id/SKU/giá sản phẩm. Mọi id là GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY: bỏ cột id khi INSERT. Thời gian là timestamptz hiển thị theo giờ Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh. Script đầy đủ: tab ctshop.sql.

Yêu cầu

  • UPDATE product SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE sku = 'CT0906' AND stock >= 1 RETURNING sku, stock.
  • Không SELECT trước UPDATE.

  CONSTRAINT customer_email_key   UNIQUE (email),

solutionCodeJson.name: query.sql
solutionCodeJson.code:
UPDATE product
SET stock = stock - 1               -- computed from the CURRENT row under its row lock
WHERE sku = 'CT0906' AND stock >= 1  -- sold out ⇒ 0 rows, no error, no negative stock
RETURNING sku, stock;

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: An UPDATE locks the row and re-reads it at its latest committed version before applying stock - 1; a concurrent UPDATE waits, then works on the new value. "Fix 1" of lesson 11.4: never read a value just to write it back.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: UPDATE khoá dòng và đọc lại phiên bản commit mới nhất trước khi áp stock - 1; UPDATE đồng thời phải chờ, rồi làm trên giá trị mới. "Cách sửa 1" của bài 11.4: đừng bao giờ đọc một giá trị chỉ để ghi nó lại.

SET TimeZone = 'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh';
CREATE TABLE customer (
  id          bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  email       text        NOT NULL,
  full_name   text        NOT NULL,
  phone       text,
  city        text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Hà Nội',
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT customer_email_key   UNIQUE (email),
  CONSTRAINT customer_email_check CHECK (email = lower(email) AND email LIKE '%_@_%.__%')
);
CREATE TABLE category (
  id         int  GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  name       text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  parent_id  int  REFERENCES category(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
);
CREATE TABLE product (
  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  sku          text          NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name         text          NOT NULL,
  category_id  int           NOT NULL REFERENCES category(id),
  price        numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (price > 0),
  stock        int           NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (stock >= 0),
  attrs        jsonb         NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  is_active    boolean       NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at   timestamptz   NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id  bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES customer(id),
  status       text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
               CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled')),
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  note         text
);
CREATE TABLE order_item (
  order_id    bigint        NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  product_id  bigint        NOT NULL REFERENCES product(id),
  qty         int           NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0),
  unit_price  numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (unit_price > 0),
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id)
);
CREATE TABLE payment (
  id        bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id  bigint        NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES orders(id),
  amount    numeric(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount > 0),
  method    text          NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('cod', 'card', 'momo', 'bank')),
  paid_at   timestamptz   NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE stock_movement (
  id          bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  product_id  bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES product(id),
  change      int         NOT NULL CHECK (change <> 0),
  reason      text        NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN ('import', 'sale', 'return', 'adjust')),
  order_id    bigint      REFERENCES orders(id),
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE TABLE review (
  id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  product_id   bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES product(id),
  customer_id  bigint      NOT NULL REFERENCES customer(id),
  rating       smallint    NOT NULL CHECK (rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  body         text,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE (product_id, customer_id)
);

exercises.title: Anatomy of a deadlock
exercises.problemHtml:
Two transfers run at the same time:

-- WINDOW 1                                        -- WINDOW 2
BEGIN;
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 10 WHERE id = 'A';
                                                   BEGIN;
                                                   UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 10 WHERE id = 'B';
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 10 WHERE id = 'B';   -- waits for window 2
                                                   UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 10 WHERE id = 'A';   -- deadlock!

Order what happens.

exercises.title: Two windows: lost update, FOR UPDATE and NOWAIT
exercises.problemHtml:
Reproduce lesson 11.4 on your own PostgreSQL with two psql windows on the accounts table (A = 100, B = 0).

-- 1) lost update: both windows
BEGIN; SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE id = 'A';          -- both read 100
UPDATE accounts SET balance = 90 WHERE id = 'A'; COMMIT;     -- window 1 (app computed 100 - 10)
UPDATE accounts SET balance = 80 WHERE id = 'A'; COMMIT;     -- window 2 (app computed 100 - 20) ⇒ 80, the -10 is lost
-- 2) the fix: SELECT … FOR UPDATE — window 2 now WAITS at its SELECT until window 1 commits, then reads 90
-- 3) don't wait: SELECT … FOR UPDATE NOWAIT  ⇒  ERROR: could not obtain lock on row (55P03)
--    or SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '2s'       ⇒  ERROR: canceling statement due to lock timeout

Runs on YOUR machine, not in the browser. Row locks only show their effect when a second session tries to take them; the browser grader has exactly one session. Nothing here is graded automatically: do the steps in your own PostgreSQL, compare with the expected output, then press Mark as solved.

Requirements

  • Part 1 ends with balance 80 (one withdrawal lost).
  • Part 2 ends with 70 (both withdrawals applied), window 2 visibly waited.
  • Part 3 shows the 55P03 or lock-timeout error instead of waiting.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: A plain SELECT never locks, so two read-modify-write transactions overwrite each other. FOR UPDATE makes the second reader wait for the first writer; NOWAIT / lock_timeout bound that wait. The simplest fix remains the atomic UPDATE of the first exercise.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: SELECT thường không khoá, nên hai giao dịch đọc-sửa-ghi đè lên nhau. FOR UPDATE khiến người đọc thứ hai chờ người ghi thứ nhất; NOWAIT / lock_timeout giới hạn thời gian chờ. Cách sửa đơn giản nhất vẫn là UPDATE nguyên tử của bài đầu.
